what: Token and cost metering reads the token counts every LLM reply already carries, turns them into money, and adds them up per user, team, customer and feature so you can set budgets and spot runaway spend.
like: Like an electricity meter with a sub-meter per room: the bill says what you spent, the sub-meters say which room did it.
why: Every call has a real price, and it grows with tokens, not with requests
Shows which tenant, feature or prompt is expensive, so you fix the right thing
Budgets and alerts stop a bug or a looping agent from burning money overnight

nodes.t: LLM API|reply has a usage block

steps.d: Your app sends the prompt along with tags: which tenant, user, feature and prompt version. Without tags you get one big bill and no idea who caused it.
Each reply reports input tokens, cached input tokens and output tokens. Reasoning (thinking) tokens are hidden from you but billed as output, so read the counts, never estimate.
Cost = each token bucket x its own price. Cached reads are much cheaper than fresh input, cache writes cost a bit more, and output usually costs most.
Add the cost to the running total for that key, team or customer. A soft limit sends a warning; a hard limit blocks the next call with a clear error.
Write one row per call to a spend log, then roll it up by tenant, model and feature. Divide by results to get cost per answer, the number product owners care about.
Watch spend per hour against a normal baseline. A sudden jump usually means a retry loop, an agent stuck calling tools, or a prompt that grew.

numbers.l: cache read price versus base input price on most Claude models
cache write price for a 5-minute cache on Claude
tokens OpenAI suggests reserving for reasoning plus output at first
input tokens where a higher long-context price tier starts (Langfuse example)

choices.d: In the app SDK, in a gateway (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Cloudflare) or in tracing (Langfuse). A gateway sees every call from every team in one place.
Pick the dimensions early: tenant, user, feature, model, prompt version. Issue one virtual key per team or customer so spend cannot be mislabelled.
Soft limit: alert at, say, 80% of budget. Hard limit: block or downgrade to a cheaper model. Choose the reset window (daily, monthly) per budget.
Prefer the provider's reported counts. Re-tokenizing text to guess cost misses hidden reasoning tokens and cache discounts.
Track cost per successful answer, per resolved ticket or per document indexed, not just total spend. It tells you if a model change was worth it.

instead.why: Full per-step traces; cost is one field on each span
General metrics stack if you only need token counters and alerts
Caps request or token rate, not money spent
Store billions of spend rows and slice them fast

breaks.d: Cost is estimated from visible text, but thinking tokens are billed as output too.
breaks.see: Your numbers sit well below the provider invoice
breaks.fix: Use the usage block from each reply, including reasoning_tokens

breaks.d: An agent keeps calling tools and the model for one task.
breaks.see: One trace with hundreds of calls; spend per hour spikes
breaks.fix: Per-task step and spend caps, plus a hard budget on the key

breaks.d: Cached reads are billed as full input, or cache writes are ignored.
breaks.see: Cost per call does not drop after you add prompt caching
breaks.fix: Separate buckets: input, cache read, cache write, output, each with its own price

breaks.t: Spend lands on the wrong tenant
breaks.d: Requests share one API key or trust a user field the client can set.
breaks.see: A big 'unknown' slice on the dashboard
breaks.fix: One virtual key per team or customer, and tags set on the server

breaks.d: A provider changes prices or adds a tier and your table does not.
breaks.see: Small but steady gap against the invoice
breaks.fix: Reconcile with the provider bill monthly and version the price table

say: Every LLM call goes through one place that reads the usage block and writes a spend row tagged with tenant, feature, model and prompt version.
Cost is tokens times price per bucket: fresh input, cached input, cache writes and output, and reasoning tokens count as output.
Each customer gets a budget with a soft alert and a hard stop, and an agent run has its own step and spend cap.
The headline metric is cost per successful answer, so we can see if a cheaper model or a cache really saved money without hurting quality.

followups.q: How do you charge customers for AI usage?
followups.a: Meter tokens per customer from the usage block, convert with a versioned price table, and add a margin or sell credits. Reconcile with the provider invoice so your totals and theirs match.

followups.q: How would you cut cost without hurting quality?
followups.a: Measure cost per answer first. Then cache stable prompt prefixes, route easy queries to a smaller model, trim retrieved context, and cap output length. Check every change against your eval set.

followups.q: What do you do when a tenant hits its budget?
followups.a: Warn at the soft limit. At the hard limit, block with a clear error, or drop to a cheaper model if the product allows. Never fail silently.

followups.q: Why not just count words to estimate cost?
followups.a: Tokenizers differ per model, cache discounts change the price, and reasoning tokens are hidden. The provider's reported counts are the only reliable source.

today: Reasoning models are now common, and their hidden thinking tokens are billed as output, so metering straight from each reply's usage block has become the standard way to track cost.

check.q: A reasoning model's reply shows only 50 words, yet the call costs a lot. Why?
check.a: Hidden reasoning tokens are billed as output
check.why: Thinking tokens are not shown but still count as output tokens.

check.q: Which is the best headline cost metric for a product team?
check.why: It ties spend to the value users get, so model and prompt changes can be judged fairly.

check.q: How do you stop one team's spend landing on another's bill?
check.a: Give each team its own virtual key and tag on the server
d: Ask users to fill in a team field
check.why: Server-side keys and tags cannot be set wrongly by a client.

check.q: A tenant reaches 80% of its monthly budget. What should happen?
d: All calls are blocked at once
check.why: Soft limits warn early; the hard limit blocks only at 100%.
